messages:
From: Greystone Bank - Procurement <procurement@greystonebank.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: RFP follow-up: request for code-assurance artifacts and remediation SLAs

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our procurement minimums we need a concise package covering your vulnerability management and code-assurance controls. Please provide the following artifacts and answers by EOD 5/18 so we can brief the security committee: 

- SAST/DAST toolset and cadence (who, frequency, ruleset/coverage).
- Penetration test summary for the most recent external assessment and confirmation of remediation of high/critical findings.
- SBOM generation cadence and scope (components vs transitive deps).
- Patch / remediation SLAs for Critical, High, Medium vulnerabilities (triage time and time-to-patch for hosted services).
- Customer options for on-demand scans (e.g., Dedicated/VPC environments).
- Any standard attestation or artifact (SOC 2, ASV scan, audit reports) you can share under NDA.

If there's a short PDF or one‑page matrix you can send that consolidates this, that would be ideal. Otherwise separate attachments are fine. Also, can you provide a short MTTR metric for the last 12 months for high/critical issues?

Regards,
Evelyn Park
Senior Procurement Analyst
Greystone Bank

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Greystone Bank - Procurement <procurement@greystonebank.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: request for code-assurance artifacts and remediation SLAs

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear list. Please find our consolidated package attached and answers inline below. I've included our security lead (Laura Bennett) and SE (Ben Carter) on the thread to support any technical follow-ups.

Attachments: Redwood_VM_Response_Greystone_v1.pdf (attached), SBOM_sample_redwood_q1_2027.csv (attached), PenTest_Summary_Redwood_2024.pdf (attached)

Summary (top-line):
- SAST: Internal static analysis runs on every PR (pre-merge) + weekly batch scans on main branches. Primary tooling: CodeSight (internal orchestration) + third-party engines (Semalytic). Coverage includes backend services, infra-as-code, and key SDKs.
- DAST: Automated DAST scans run nightly against staging and before releases; authenticated DAST for sessioned endpoints is used for changes to the runtime. Tooling: WebProbe (internal) + third-party ASV for external-facing surfaces.
- Pen test: External red-team conducted by RedQuartz in Nov 2024. High/critical findings were tracked in our ticketing system; all high/critical issues were mitigated and verified; summary attached.
- SBOM: We produce component-level SBOMs every quarter and an on-demand transitive SBOM upon customer request. SBOMs include package, version, license, and sha256.
- Patch / remediation SLAs (hosted): Triage for Critical: within 72 hours; remediation target: 7–14 days depending on exploitability and customer impact. High: triage within 5 business days, remediation target 30 days. Medium/Low: standard release cadence or backport as needed. For Dedicated customers we offer faster remediation windows as a contractual option.
- On-demand scans: Yes — Dedicated and Private customers can request in-place scanning; for Dedicated we can run scans in-customer-network (with customer approval) or provide artifacts from our scans.

MTTR (12mo): We track from detection to verified remediation. Per last 12 months: Critical (verified) median MTTR = 11 days; High median MTTR = 27 days. Full CSV with monthly breakdown attached (greystone_mttr_12mo.csv).

Next steps: happy to do a 30–45 minute call with the security committee to walk through the artifacts. Suggested times: Mon 5/24 AM PT or Tue 5/25.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Stephanie —

Thank you for the materials. Quick clarifying questions before we route to legal/security committee: 

1) The MTTR numbers look reasonable — can you confirm whether the MTTR figures exclude cases where a third‑party vendor (OS package) had to issue a patch and you were awaiting the vendor patch?
2) For the pen test summary: can you confirm that all high/critical findings have a verification ticket and timeline in Jira (we may request export of the ticket IDs under NDA)?
3) SBOM cadence: quarterly is fine — is there an automated push to customers (e.g., via secure link) or is this manual?
4) For the remediation SLA language we propose adding a clause that requires notification within 24 hours for customer-impacting Critical issues — can you accommodate a 24-hour notification commitment?

Also copy to our legal lead (legal@greystonebank.com) will happen soon — they'll ask for standard vulnerability disclosure and notification language.

Best,
Evelyn

Stephanie / Laura —

Thanks — answers below (copied back to Evelyn in the reply we will send). Attaching the MTTR breakdown and a sanitized ticket export for RedQuartz findings.

1) MTTR scope: Our MTTR figures exclude vendor-pending patch windows. We record those separately as "3rd-party dependency delay" and they are not counted against Redwood remediation clocks. I included a column in greystone_mttr_12mo.csv that marks vendor_wait = true/false per incident.

2) Pen test evidence: RedQuartz high/critical findings were ingested into Jira and have remediation tickets. We created a sanitized export (ticket IDs, finding severity, remediation date) suitable for sharing under NDA (attached: remediation_ticket_export.csv). Each exported ticket includes a verification timestamp from our QA team.

3) SBOM delivery: We publish quarterly SBOMs to a secure S3 bucket and can optionally push to a customer SFTP/URL on request. We also produce on-demand transitive SBOMs within 3 business days of request.

4) 24-hour notification: Operationally we can commit to notification (acknowledgement + initial triage summary) within 24 hours for customer-impacting Critical issues. Full remediation targets remain as previously stated; for contract language we recommend: 24-hour notification + 72-hour triage window + remediation as per classification (with accelerated options for Dedicated). If Legal wants to tighten to an absolute patch window, we can review on a per-deal basis.

Attachments included for Greystone: greystone_mttr_12mo.csv, remediation_ticket_export.csv, remediation_plan_slide_deck.pptx

I'll send the consolidated reply to Evelyn and include the attachments under an NDA link.

Ben Carter
